title: Enigmatic Book of the Solar-Osirian Unity: second gilded shrine of Tutankhamun (Carter 237) and tomb of Ramesses IX (KV 6). Egyptian enigmatic (cryptographic) writing, not a cipher in the usual sense; one pre-registered measured check of the convention, failed its threshold

system.summary: Not a cipher in the usual sense, and not classical hieroglyphic writing either: Egyptian enigmatic (cryptographic) writing, a learned sign-substitution convention of New Kingdom netherworld books. No secret key: most signs keep their ordinary value and a minority are replaced by other signs on scribal rules (acrophony, look-alike signs, rare spellings); the language is ordinary Egyptian. The same monuments also carry texts in ordinary hieroglyphs, which were not measured.
system.notes: Values learned on exposed blocks (C03-C12), table v5: kneeling man / bar = n; hills / trapeze = h (acrophony of h3st); S28 = s; double reed / two strokes = y; V13 = t; wick = h; slope = q; three dots = plural; forked bar = w; arrow = p. About one sign in four substituted on the Ramesses IX register 2 line (C11). Homophones: several shapes write n, and several write h. Values found only after the C13 measure (table v6, frozen in C14, never measured): knob = p, slanted flagpole = ntr, inverted hill = dw, V6 = sh by acrophony.

solution.what: Learned a sign-substitution table on an exposed block (shrine pl. IV, 17-column text, aligned on Piankoff's published transliteration).
Exploratory tests in C03-C12 on other shrine and Ramesses IX passages; some frozen before comparison, some not (C07 knew Darnell's general translation). Not used as evidence of success.

Pre-registered single measurement of the frozen table v5 on a held-out 428-sign portion no session had read (269 Ramesses IX + 159 shrine signs). Reference values aligned after the blind reading was frozen, from Darnell & Darnell 2018, by a separate model run that did not see the table. M = 27/65 = 0.415 against 200 permuted tables (best 0.154, mean 0.018); bar 0.70 and best + 0.30: FAILED. Secondary, no decision: substitution entries 18/26, ordinary values 9/39; Ramesses IX 27/58, shrine 0/7.

Unit-level reading after comparison (37 units): 1 sure (xpr, Khepri), 3 probable (xprw 'manifestations'; Hr 'face'; Ra ... nb), 12 restored from the publication, 21 unresolved. The repeated snake legend was predicted blind as one repeated name (structure only; the word, 'One Who Is Shot', is Darnell's).

C14: table v6 frozen with the four values found after C13, but no unused enigmatic portion of 300 signs remains in Guilmant's plates (the only unread text, pl. LXXVIII-LXXIX, about 120 signs, is ordinary hieroglyphs). No measurement made.

outcome.method_basis: The texts are read and published by Darnell (2004; with Manassa Darnell 2018). This project did not obtain the text: its frozen substitution table was measured once on a held-out portion and failed the pre-set bar (0.415 < 0.70), although far above the permuted controls. The table-only output is 'decoded, not read' on the repository's definitions, so no outcome.texts entry and no reading_review grade are recorded (see NOTES.md, Reading review). The permutation test (200 permuted tables) is reported in NOTES.md; it was not run through docs/_validate.py, so verification stays 'none'.
outcome.fraction_read_source: C13 measurement (working files outside the repository): 27 of the 428 held-out signs were given a value that the reference confirms. The table gives some value to 301/428 (70 %), but only 65 could be checked against the reference and 27 were right. Three units: M = 27/65 (pre-registered measure, checkable signs only); fraction_read = 27/428 (all held-out signs, unchecked ones counted unread); fraction_coherent = 1/37 (read rule, sure words only, probable and restored units counted as holes). See NOTES.md, Reading.
